name: ICL8038
description: Monolithic function generator that produces simultaneous sine, square, and triangle wave outputs from 0.001Hz to 300kHz, set by external R/C and adjustable duty cycle (2%-98%). A classic analog-synth and test-equipment building block. Marked 'NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS' by Intersil, but remains widely used and second-sourced given its unique combined three-waveform output. Known in practice for sine-wave distortion and part-to-part variation that often needs trimming (external THD-adjust network) to hit datasheet-spec sine purity.

pins.name: DUTY CYCLE
pins.description: duty cycle / frequency adjust resistor terminal

pins.name: FREQ ADJ
pins.description: duty cycle / frequency adjust resistor terminal

pins.name: FM SWEEP
pins.description: FM sweep input, for voltage-controlled frequency

pins.name: SQUARE OUT
pins.description: square wave output (open collector, needs a pullup)

pins.name: SINE ADJ2
pins.description: sine wave adjust (distortion trim, second terminal)

DIP-14.notes: Per Intersil's own pinout diagram, PDIP/CERDIP, top view.

typical_application: Analog synth VCOs and LFOs, function generators, FM modulators, and test equipment needing simultaneous sine/square/triangle outputs from one chip.
gotchas: SQUARE OUT (pin 9) is open-collector; it needs an external pullup resistor to work
sine output distortion is a known practical issue; many designs add an external trim network on the SINE ADJ pins to hit low-THD sine output, do not expect clean sine out of the box without it
marked NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS by Intersil; still in wide use and second-sourced, this is not a sign the part is fake, just that the manufacturer prefers customers move to newer parts
duty cycle and frequency are both set by the same external R/C network and interact; changing one without accounting for the other shifts both
